_doc:
FOG (Phase 053): what a fogged resident knows of the map, in three levels. 0 hidden: nothing known, not even that it exists. 1 vague: the structure, meaning named places (landmarks, named buildings, area names) and roughly where they are, with the paths between known places. 2 full: the ground cell by cell (remembered terrain and whether people were seen there), and the exact place. The rules and words here are read by domains/map_memory.py; the world publishes physical facts only, and the resident's map is held by the resident (a MemoryRecord of kind map_memory).

FOG_RULES. exact_radius: the cells around an exact place's cell that are known at level 2 at founding (a home or a workplace). landmark_sight: a named place within this many cells becomes level 1 even beyond sight_range (Phase 028's HEARING.sight_range is the level-2 radius each turn). stale_ticks: a remembered cell or place not seen for this many clock ticks is said to be remembered, not seen (TIME: 96 ticks a day, so 288 is three days). explore_steps: how far ahead a compass heading (`toward north`) aims, in cells. near_landmark_cells: a place is described as near another known place within this distance. max_labels: the most places the view lists. label_letters: the glyphs of the labels, in order. All of these are APPROX model choices, not measured figures; their order of magnitude is set by the 52 by 40 founding town.

FOG_PUBLIC_LANDMARKS: places every resident knows at level 1 from the start (the market, the church, the well), whatever their history. The names are keys of the founding layout (FOUNDING_WORKPLACES, FOUNDING_BUILDING_SITES, FOUNDING_MAP's square). The hamlet has no founding sites, so its list is empty.

FOG_PLACE_WORDS: the words for a place by its name, where the founding labels (FOUNDING_PLACE_LABELS) do not give them. Other places are worded from FOUNDING_PLACE_LABELS, or from the name itself. Words are fixed phrases with no digit.

FOG_WORDS. directions: the eight compass headings in order from north, clockwise, with the word for each. distances: the bands of distance in cells (Chebyshev), in order; a band with direction false gives the phrase alone. ages: the bands of time since a cell or place was last seen, in clock ticks, in order. label, label_rough, label_near, remembered, path_between, spot: the sentence templates. Every band is a rough word, never a count.

SOURCES. None: every figure and phrase is an APPROX authored choice. The compass headings and the distance and age words are conventions of English, not a measurement.
